subject: S3 routing + revenue share — technical appendix and next steps
messages:
From: Tom Saunders <tom@pinecone.io>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-27T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Partner pilot: S3 routing + revshare proposal

Karthik / Vanessa —

Thanks for the sync earlier. Elena and I reviewed the integration notes and we like the idea of a lightweight routing layer that directs cold-fallthrough queries to VectorGrid's S3-backed index while hot queries stay on Pinecone. Before we lock commercials, can you confirm:

- Would Redwood be comfortable routing requests based on index TTL and a routing header (x-index-tier)?
- How do you want failures handled if VectorGrid S3 is slow — automatic retry to Pinecone or return a graceful degraded result?

I've attached a short revshare term sheet (revshare_term_sheet_v1.pdf) and a diagram (s3-routing-arch.vsdx). At a high level VectorGrid proposes 20% take of throughput revenue on queries routed to their store for the first 12 months of the pilot; we can re-open after pilot KPIs.

Can we get a technical appendix from Redwood that lays out error handling, retry policy, and expected latency SLOs when routing to a cold tier?

- Tom
Senior Partnerships, Pinecone

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Tom Saunders <tom@pinecone.io>, Elena Ruiz <elena@vectorgrid.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-27T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partner pilot: S3 routing + revshare proposal

Tom / Elena —

Appreciate the clear proposal. Quick answers and next steps below.

1) Routing header: yes — we can support an x-index-tier header to prefer hot vs cold. For pilot we recommend Redwood own routing decisions with a transparent decision tree we publish to partners (TTL, recency, and cache-hit rate).

2) Failure handling: default behavior will be a 2-attempt retry to VectorGrid with exponential backoff; if still failing within our per-request latency envelope (configurable per-customer), we will fallback to a partial result from Pinecone if a fallback index exists, otherwise we return a 503 with a structured error that callers can interpret to optionally degrade the UI. We'll include a canary override to force immediate fallback for customer acceptance testing.

3) Latency SLOs: cold tier target is median 220ms additional tail beyond hot (99th under 1.5s for routed calls in US region during pilot baseline). These are pilot targets and will be validated during the first two weeks with synthetic load.

I've attached a draft pilot runbook (pilot-runbook.md) and noted where we need your infra contacts to provide presigned-routing keys and sample S3 object manifests.

Next steps:
- Vanessa: take lead on operational runbook and support matrix (can you own?).
- Ben: will scope observability hooks and per-route cost telemetry.
- VectorGrid: confirm revshare percentage and any minimum monthly guarantee.

If we can lock technical appendix and a commercial one-pager by EOD Friday we can route to Sales Ops and Legal for an expedited pilot MOU.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@vectorgrid.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Tom Saunders <tom@pinecone.io>
Cc: Jake Morris <jake.morris@vectorgrid.ai>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-28T09:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partner pilot: S3 routing + revshare proposal

Karthik / Team —

Thanks — confirms on our side. A few clarifications from VectorGrid:

- Revshare: we can accept 20% on routed throughput for months 1–6, then step down to 15% month 7–12 if pilot KPIs (latency, error rate, cost delta) are met. We'd prefer no minimum for the pilot but ask for a commitment to a joint post-pilot commercial review.

- Failover: we want automatic fallback to Pinecone when possible (best-effort merge of nearest-neighbor results), but if fallback would significantly degrade quality we prefer a structured error so the product can show a cached answer. We'll share an algorithm doc for partial-merge semantics.

- Data residency: S3 objects for VectorGrid will live in customers' buckets. We'll need Redwood to support conditional presigned access for read-only fetches and to surface the bucket-region in routing decisions.

We'll sign the revshare term sheet draft and send back comments inline — expect that later today. Can someone on Redwood confirm the expected CloudTrail/audit events we need to collect for usage reconciliation?

— Elena
Head of Partnerships, VectorGrid

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@vectorgrid.ai>, Tom Saunders <tom@pinecone.io>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-29T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partner pilot: S3 routing + revshare proposal

Thanks all — short operational commitments from Redwood:

- Observability: we will emit per-route token-attribution and a routed_tier label (hot|cold) to our telemetry pipeline. Ben will add a reconciliation export (daily CSV) for usage-based revshare checks.
- Reconciliation events: CloudTrail-style logs we need: s3:getObject (with presigned-request-id), routing-decision-id, request-latency-ms, fallback-flag. We'll publish the event schema by EOD 2027-07-01.
- Security: presigned URLs will be used; no long-lived credentials. We will sign an NDA addendum for bucket access.
- Pilot timeline: 2-week integration window + 30-day validation window. Go/no-go review at day 45.

Attached: revshare_term_sheet_v1.pdf (updated comments), pilot-runbook.md (integration checklist). Jake — please review the runbook notes about manifest formatting and presign lifecycle and confirm you can deliver sample manifests by 2027-07-02.

I'll open a short DocuSign for the MOU after we incorporate your inline comments.

— Vanessa
Head of Partnerships Operations, Redwood Inference
